title: Machine learning-assisted prediction of pneumonia based on non-invasive measures
summary: A retrospective single-center cohort of 535 lower-respiratory-illness patients was classified as pneumonia versus bronchitis from non-invasive measures; the authors report cross-validated and held-out model performance. This is diagnostic evidence on the study sample, not prospective or clinical-utility validation.
ai_technology: Eight machine-learning classifiers distinguish pneumonia from bronchitis using clinical and laboratory measures.
organization: College of Public Health, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, China

evidence.tested: The paper reports experiments on 535 patients and performance metrics for RF/XGBoost on original and resampled data, with pneumonia/bronchitis as outcome classes.
evidence.unknown: The study reports five-fold cross-validation and an 80/20 training/test split on a retrospective single-center sample. This supports a bounded diagnostic-model result, but not generalization or clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Eight machine-learning classifiers distinguish pneumonia from bronchitis using clinical and laboratory measures.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
